beats.care: If an ad or influencer promises guaranteed or risk-free market returns, that breaks the rules. Treat it as a red flag.
beats.what: SEBI has notified a common advertising code for brokers, mutual funds, investment advisers and others, published in the official gazette on 9 October.
beats.why: Celebrity ads are now allowed for a firm's brand, but each needs approval first and can't make claims about a specific product.

cards.body: Influencers count as celebrities once their followers on one platform cross the limit set by ad watchdog ASCI. Founders promoting their own company don't count. The code doesn't cover crypto or prediction-market ads.

Market investments can rise or fall, so nobody can honestly guarantee a return. Lines like 'double your money' pull beginners into risks they don't understand. Online bond platforms are the one exception.
cards.title: why ban return promises?

cards.body: Firms also can't charge clients or fund investors for the celebrity's fee.

watch: The rules take effect 180 days after their 9 October notification, so around April 2027.
